heroHeadline: US Withholds Burhan's UN Visa Over Ceasefire Rejection as Sudan's Army Presses North Kordofan Offensive
heroSubtitle: A diplomatic crisis erupted around the UN General Assembly this week: US advisor Massad Boulos met Egyptian and Sudanese foreign ministers in New York on September 20, 2026 to press for a durable peace path, then the State Department withheld Sovereignty Council chief Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan's UNGA visa on September 22, tying it to a 90-day ceasefire Burhan rejected as a take-it-or-leave-it proposal — spokesman Tommy Pigott declared that neither SAF nor RSF have legitimate authority to rule Sudan, saying both 'rule through force of arms alone.' Sudan's UN ambassador asked Secretary-General Guterres to intervene, and on September 23 Burhan published a Foreign Policy op-ed proposing a Sudanese-led alternative centered on a single unified national army and rejecting political parity for the RSF. The diplomacy unfolded against continued fighting on the ground: a Rapid Support Forces attack on the Umm Badr gold market in North Kordofan killed five civilians and wounded 27 on September 21, days after the army's September 17 and 19 recapture of a dozen North Kordofan areas including the al-Jamama commercial hub. Day 1258 of the SAF-RSF war with no ceasefire and famine conditions persisting across Darfur and Kordofan.
